narr: A low pressure system located across eastern New Mexico brought in an abundance of moisture aloft to the southern and western Texas Panhandle. The high amounts of moisture provided by the low pressure system created a tropical type environment allowing heavy rain showers to develop and move from southeast to northwest across the southern Texas Panhandle. Although the instability was limited, the lift from the low pressure system combined with abnormally high moisture led to rain rates upwards of 1 to 2 inches per hour. These heavy rains fell over an area that had already received over 1 of rainfall earlier in the morning and just over 2 the day before. These rain rates on top of the unique terrain of the canyon contributed to flash flooding that other areas in the Texas Panhandle would otherwise not see. The flash flood conditions caused a few motorists to be stranded and they had to be rescued due to the fast flowing water across some of the roadways. Parts of the canyon had also already received just over 2 the day before and with an additional 4 to 5 by mid afternoon.
ev: Water rescues were conducted due to flash flooding in the park. Pictures were provided to the NWS Amarillo through social media that depicted water over roadways with stalled cars.
